title: Bennewitz sees craft at Kirtland
place_text: Kirtland Air Force Base, New Mexico

tellings.quote: like even him like the reason that he got onto the radar of all these kind of like counter intel people was because he saw this craft, you know, vertically taking off and landing at Kirtland Air Force Base
sighting things over. There's a a mountain out in the desert at Kirtland Air Force Base called Manzano Mountain and they store nuclear weapons there. He'd sighted UFOs flying over there a lot.
tellings.difference: Places the sightings over Manzano Mountain, where nuclear weapons are stored, and says they happened often, where the story describes a single craft taking off and landing vertically.
tellings.link_reason: Both are about Bennewitz seeing UFOs at Kirtland AFB.

as_told.title: Bennewitz's UFO sightings over Manzano Mountain
as_told.place_text: Manzano Mountain, Kirtland Air Force Base, New Mexico

tellings.quote: he was seeing lights like out out somewhere on the base like lifting up off the ground and flying over a mountain and going down. They were they were glowing orbs
tellings.difference: Calls the objects glowing orbs flying over a mountain, not a craft taking off vertically, and dates it 1977-1978 rather than 1979.
tellings.link_reason: Both tell of Bennewitz watching objects take off and land at Kirtland AFB, the sighting that brought him to counterintelligence attention.

as_told.title: Benowitz sees glowing orbs rising from Kirtland AFB
as_told.place_text: Kirtland Air Force Base, Albuquerque, New Mexico

plain: In the late 1970s a civilian named Paul Bennewitz, living near Kirtland Air Force Base in New Mexico, says he saw strange craft rising and landing on the base. Jesse Michels says this is what put Bennewitz on the radar of military counter-intelligence people: he saw a craft "vertically taking off and landing at Kirtland Air Force Base." The physicist John Brandenburg repeats what Bennewitz said, placing the sightings over Manzano Mountain, a mountain at the base where nuclear weapons are stored, and saying he saw UFOs there a lot. The writer Greg Bishop, who researched Bennewitz's story, describes the objects as "glowing orbs" lifting off the ground somewhere on the base, flying over a mountain and coming down. Bishop dates it to 1977 and 1978 rather than 1979. The tellers tell it because UFOs over a nuclear weapons site would be a serious matter, and because of what the government did to Bennewitz afterwards.
